title: The hypercube Ramsey number has linear order
main_claim: There is an absolute constant C with R(Q_n) <= C 2^n for all n, which would settle the Burr-Erdos cube question. The proof is by contradiction. It assumes a counterexample sequence with N/2^n -> infinity, derives two-sided discrepancy, tiles the cube by prefix subcubes over extracted patches, and finishes the low modes with late syndrome-class replacement and a two-endpoint Hall estimate.

prior_single_reviewer:
The paper is about 9,900 lines of dense LaTeX across 18 sections (build/sections/*.tex). I could not referee all of it, so the verdict is could_not_assess rather than a clean pass. Every step below that I checked holds up, and I found no gap in it.

Checked:
- Intro lower bound (3*2^{n-1}-1) and the Graham-Rodl-Rucinski arithmetic, 8(16n)^n.
- Lemma 2.1, the counterexample-sequence reduction.
- Section 3 tools: the stabilization/diagonalization lemma, balanced mixtures (the separation argument with K=4/kappa, and the Kakutani profile argument), the conditional LLL avoidance comparison, the scattered-moments expansion and the gated-posterior lemma.
- Section 10: the Hamming-syndrome projection (H' preimages, multiplicity 2 or H', parity toggle) and the compatibility of the parameter chain m=n^{200d}, k=n^{300d}, T=n^{141d} with the height-lemma constraints (b0>a>zeta+sigma+1-theta, b>a+4sigma, b>b0+(D+1)rho with D=6, k(T+m)=o(n^{eta0})).
- Section 13 in full: the residual-scale bounds, including the codegree identity (1+m+m'+K)/4 and the reduction to a full-dimensional cluster witness; the direct-mode 1/8-7/8 averaging (11/16 checked); dyadic rounding to an exact sum of 1 with sum_J M_i > S/2; the role counts; and the h_i, l_i < n^iota bounds.
- Section 16: the late syndrome classes (full rank of (s, parity), class size 2^{n-1}/H_*, the floor(j/2)..j neighbor counts, at most one internal late neighbor) and the fit of cell and slot counts using C_n -> infinity.
- Section 18: the e_{w,j} budget and the cap (source-25), and the final two-endpoint Hall lemma (component counting, the 2M(K/M)^{p-2}(M^{-2}e^{.01n})^2 bound, and the large-set bound M(K/C_n)^{eta n}, which is eventually negative however slowly C_n grows).

Not verified: Sections 4-9, 11, 12, 14, 15 and 17, and the bulk of Section 18 (transfer, terminal avoidance, late assignment, joint endpoint kernels). The decisive probabilistic estimates live there; I accepted their stated outputs as inputs to what I checked.
